saw.short: Celebrity Traitors fans spend a week hunting clues before the finale
saw.headline: Celebrity Traitors fans spent the week *hunting clues*
saw.what: Fans treated tiny details as evidence, such as King Kenny's pen position, which some read as a clue to who was next. The finale is tonight at 8pm on BBC One, with Uncloaked at 9.20pm.
saw.why: Fans do the guessing, so every episode restarts the theories. Tonight is the peak.

saw.short: Bradley Walsh's mystery quiz is explained, and it airs on Sunday
saw.headline: Bradley Walsh's *mystery quiz* is explained
saw.what: A live-TV-only trailer had people guessing. Channel 4's synopsis, out on Wednesday, says contestants bring their own bank cards and bet cash on general-knowledge questions, winning “Bet Balls” they can cash out or fire into the “Million Pound Shot Machine” for £1m. It's a one-off on Sunday at 9pm.
saw.why: The mystery trailer did its job: people guessed, then the format landed days before the show.

saw.short: Asda's £30-off deal becomes a half-price video game hack
saw.headline: Asda's £30-off deal becomes a *half-price game hack*
saw.what: Asda offered £30 off a £60+ shop to first-time online customers who sign up to marketing emails. It worked on electronics, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 at half price. By Tuesday 27 Oct Asda had paused it, citing “a significant number of orders that do not qualify”.
saw.why: Promo terms get tested in public within days, and receipts and how-to videos become the content.

saw.short: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or in London, after a website leak
saw.headline: Harry Kane wins the *Ballon d'Or* in London
saw.what: Harry Kane won on Monday, the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001. Hours earlier the awards website wrongly published articles naming Kane, Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal each as winner. Organisers said the profiles were “inadvertently published”.
saw.why: A British winner and an accidental leak gave people two reasons to post.

saw.short: Just Eat's AI menu photos get ridiculed, then paused
saw.headline: Just Eat's *AI menu photos* get ridiculed, then paused
saw.what: Just Eat's AI-made dish photos went viral: bacon-and-egg soda bread became a glass of cola with an egg and bacon in it, and garlic bread became a plane. Just Eat said “We're sorry for any inaccurate images that have been posted” and paused the rollout.
saw.why: The gap between the picture and the real dish became the joke. Real photos beat AI that gets it wrong.
saw.source: Dexerto, 23 Oct (citing the BBC and The Journal)

saw.short: The niche Halloween costume meme is back, a day before Halloween
saw.headline: The *niche Halloween costume* meme is back
saw.what: The annual format is back on X: people caption deep-cut costume ideas, such as Dakota Johnson and limes or Princess Diana's revenge dress. The Tab, citing Know Your Meme, traces it to 2022–2023, and it went massively viral in 2024. Halloween is tomorrow.
saw.why: The more obscure the costume, the better the post. Brands can play with deep cuts from their own world.

platform.short: Meta pushes its new business terms back to 20 Nov
platform.headline: Meta *pushes back* its business terms to 20 Nov
platform.what: Meta moved its new commercial terms from 30 Oct to 20 Nov “to allow more time for us to explain”, after complaints from publishers and advertisers to EU and UK antitrust authorities. Critics say the terms give Meta broad rights to use content for AI. Meta rejects that.
platform.why: Anything planned around 30 Oct can wait. The dispute is about AI training rights over business content.

platform.short: Instagram tests 90-minute videos with select US creators
platform.headline: Instagram tests *90-minute videos* with US creators
platform.what: Instagram has begun testing “Features”: uploads of up to 90 minutes, such as podcasts and vlogs, with select US creators. Creators can link Reels clips to the full video, and it isn't exclusive to Instagram. No UK date has been given.
platform.why: Instagram is going after long-form video. Don't plan around it in the UK yet.

platform.short: Discord will put public server messages into Google
platform.headline: Discord will put *public server messages* into Google
platform.what: From 16 Nov, Discord will create public web pages for big “Discoverable Servers”. From mid-December, messages in eligible public channels may appear there and in search. In the UK a user setting is off by default, so messages show only if people opt in.
platform.why: Public community chat becomes searchable. Brands with open Discords should check what's on show.
